```{r QD_Parameter_Threshold_Analysis_and_Visualisation, eval = params$run_filtration_parameters, fig.width = 11.69, fig.height = 8.27, out.width = "100%"}
### 3. Plot Score margin
margin_reads <- read_tsv(asp_reads_path,
                         col_select = c(locus, called_allele, score_margin, snp_position_quality, tie_flag, below_threshold_flag),
                         col_types = cols(locus = "c", called_allele = "c", score_margin = "d", snp_position_quality = "i",
                                          tie_flag = "l", below_threshold_flag = "l")) %>%
  mutate(fate = case_when(!is.na(called_allele) ~ "Used for genotyping", # why a read was not used, same groups and colours as in the Sankey
                          tie_flag ~ "No allele signal (tie)",
                          below_threshold_flag ~ "Poor alignment",
                          TRUE ~ "Failed a SNP check"))

# the highest margin one read can reach (about 7.88 at primer Q19). Its the margin of every perfect-quality read, so the largest value in the data is exactly that ceiling
margin_max <- max(margin_reads$score_margin, na.rm = TRUE)
margin_frac_under_cutoff <- mean(margin_reads$score_margin < margin_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE) # reads where the primers barely differ, so ties

# margin per read as a fraction of the maximum margin is what each read adds to QD, two panels for used and not used.
margin_fate_colours <- c(`Used for genotyping` = correct_colour, `Failed a SNP check` = "#7F919B",
                         `No allele signal (tie)` = "#A6453A", `Poor alignment` = "#C97B3D")
margin_panel_names <- c(sprintf("Used for genotyping (%s reads)", comma(sum(margin_reads$fate == "Used for genotyping"))),
                        sprintf("Not used (%s reads), by reason", comma(sum(margin_reads$fate != "Used for genotyping"))))

margin_plot_data <- margin_reads %>%
  filter(!is.na(score_margin)) %>%
  mutate(evidence = score_margin / margin_max,
         panel = factor(ifelse(fate == "Used for genotyping", margin_panel_names[1], margin_panel_names[2]), levels = margin_panel_names),
         fate = factor(fate, levels = names(margin_fate_colours)))

# Q ladder for the top axis: each bar is one base quality at the SNP, the margin is basically just the SNP and its quality determines the steps. Lower quality has longer breaks because the scoring differs more with lower quality, highers scores barely change so the bars are closer.
margin_min_snp_quality <- min_snp_quality # min_snp_quality of the ASP run, reads below it fail the SNP check
margin_q_ladder <- margin_plot_data %>%
  filter(score_margin > 0, !is.na(snp_position_quality)) %>%
  group_by(snp_quality = snp_position_quality) %>%
  summarise(evidence = median(evidence), .groups = "drop")
margin_q_axis <- filter(margin_q_ladder, snp_quality %in% c(5, 10, 15, 20, 30))
margin_q_cutoff <- margin_q_ladder$evidence[margin_q_ladder$snp_quality == margin_min_snp_quality] 

# Plot
p_score_margin_by_pass <- ggplot(margin_plot_data, aes(x = evidence, fill = fate)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = margin_q_cutoff, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.01, boundary = 1, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) + 
  facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25), expand = expansion(add = 0.01),
                     sec.axis = dup_axis(breaks = margin_q_axis$evidence, labels = paste0("Q", margin_q_axis$snp_quality), name = NULL)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = margin_fate_colours, name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Margin per read: used vs. rejected reads",
       x = "Score margin per read as a fraction of the maximum margin",
       y = "Number of reads")+
  theme_minimal(base_family = plot_font, base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "grey30", size = 9, lineheight = 1.1),
        plot.caption.position = "plot",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, hjust = 0),
        strip.placement = "outside", 
        axis.text.x.top = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
        axis.ticks.x.top = element_line(colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.4), 
        axis.ticks.length.x.top = unit(3, "pt"),
        legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
print(p_score_margin_by_pass)
ggsave(file.path(qd_asp_dir, "score_margin_by_pass_status.png"), p_score_margin_by_pass, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(qd_asp_dir, "score_margin_by_pass_status.pdf"), p_score_margin_by_pass, width = 8, height = 6, device = cairo_pdf)


### 4. Plot: Ties and worst loci

# Plot shows fraction of reads with a near-zero margin per loci. A score_margin below margin_cutoff is almost only the ties at 0 of the score margin plot, so this is the "no allele signal" rate
margin_locus_summary <- margin_reads %>%
  group_by(locus) %>%
  summarise(n_reads = n(),
            n_near_zero_margin = sum(score_margin < margin_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_score_margin = median(score_margin, na.rm = TRUE),
            frac_near_zero_margin_locus = mean(score_margin < margin_cutoff, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

# The box plot outlier rule, upper quartile + 1.5 x interquartile range.
margin_outlier_threshold <- unname(quantile(margin_locus_summary$frac_near_zero_margin_locus, 0.75) +
                                     1.5 * IQR(margin_locus_summary$frac_near_zero_margin_locus))

# Data prep for loci above the outlier threshold
margin_locus_summary <- margin_locus_summary %>%
  mutate(flagged = frac_near_zero_margin_locus > margin_outlier_threshold) %>% 
  arrange(desc(frac_near_zero_margin_locus)) 

margin_flagged_loci <- margin_locus_summary$locus[margin_locus_summary$flagged]
margin_worst_locus <- margin_locus_summary[1, ]
margin_line_n_each <- 3 # other loci used for line plot, the first 3 below the flagged ones and the last 3

# rows from the top: flagged loci (bars), the next loci (line), the break, the last loci (line)
margin_other_loci <- filter(margin_locus_summary, !flagged)
margin_has_break <- nrow(margin_other_loci) > 2 * margin_line_n_each + 1 # only break the line when there are enough loci

margin_line_loci <- if (margin_has_break) {
  bind_rows(mutate(head(margin_other_loci, margin_line_n_each), line_part = "first"), # if true, selects first and last
            mutate(tail(margin_other_loci, margin_line_n_each), line_part = "last"))
} else mutate(margin_other_loci, line_part = "first")

# Ordering of the display
margin_display <- bind_rows(filter(margin_locus_summary, flagged), margin_line_loci) %>%
  mutate(row = row_number() + (margin_has_break & line_part %in% "last")) # the last part one row lower, the gap row stays empty
margin_n_rows <- max(margin_display$row)
margin_display <- mutate(margin_display, y = margin_n_rows - row + 1) 

# Label and miscall tag only for the flagged loci
margin_flagged_labels <- margin_display %>%
  filter(flagged) %>%
  left_join(asp_results %>%
              filter(locus %in% margin_flagged_loci) %>%
              left_join(ref %>% select(barcode = sample, locus, reference_genotype = genotype), by = c("barcode", "locus")) %>%
              group_by(locus) %>%
              summarise(n_miscalled = sum(genotype != reference_genotype, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"), 
            by = "locus") %>%
  mutate(bar_label = sprintf("%.1f%% (%s / %s)", 100 * frac_near_zero_margin_locus,
                             comma(n_near_zero_margin), comma(n_reads)),
         miscall_tag = ifelse(n_miscalled == 0, "no miscalls", sprintf("%d miscalled", n_miscalled)))

# Sequence around the SNP for every locus in the plot, on the strand the ASP primers read
margin_context_left <- 14 # bases shown before the SNP (the primer side, where a homopolymer shifts the SNP)
margin_context_right <- 4 # bases shown after the SNP (about the anchor bases)
margin_reference <- readDNAStringSet(reference_path)
names(margin_reference) <- sub("::.*$", "", names(margin_reference)) 
margin_panel_sheet <- readxl::read_excel(primer_panel_path, sheet = "Final panel", .name_repair = "minimal") 
margin_panel <- tibble(locus = margin_panel_sheet[["SNP name"]],
                       asp1 = trimws(margin_panel_sheet[["ASP1_SEQ (forward allele1)"]]),
                       asp2 = trimws(margin_panel_sheet[["ASP2_SEQ (forward allele2)"]])) %>%
  filter(locus %in% margin_display$locus)

margin_context_f <- function(locus, asp1, asp2) {
  if (!locus %in% names(margin_reference)) return(c(context = "not in reference", homopolymer = ""))
  body <- DNAString(substr(asp1, 1, nchar(asp1) - 1)) # primer without its SNP base
  for (strand in c("+", "-")) {
    s <- if (strand == "+") margin_reference[[locus]] else reverseComplement(margin_reference[[locus]]) # the reference, or its reverse complement for the second try
    hit <- matchPattern(body, s, max.mismatch = 2)
    hit <- matchPattern(body, s, max.mismatch = 2)
    if (length(hit) == 1) {
      snp <- end(hit) + 1 
      left <- as.character(subseq(s, max(1, snp - margin_context_left), snp - 1))
      right <- as.character(subseq(s, snp + 1, min(length(s), snp + margin_context_right)))
      alleles <- c(substring(asp1, nchar(asp1)), substring(asp2, nchar(asp2)))
      before <- as.character(subseq(s, max(1, snp - 30), snp - 1))
      after <- as.character(subseq(s, snp + 1, min(length(s), snp + 30)))
      # homopolymer before the SNP (the primer's 3' end): a length error in this run moves the read by one base, so the
      # SNP position holds a neighbouring base that matches neither allele = tie. "C×5+C" = the C allele continues the run
      before_base <- substring(before, nchar(before))
      before_run <- attr(regexpr(paste0(before_base, "+$"), before), "match.length")
      before_tag <- if (before_run >= 3) paste0(before_base, "\u00d7", before_run, if (before_base %in% alleles) paste0("+", before_base) else "") else ""
      # homopolymer after the SNP, only when an allele continues it ("C+C×7"): the SNP base is then the first base of the run,
      # and a missing base in the run is placed at the run start = the SNP position
      after_base <- substr(after, 1, 1)
      after_run <- attr(regexpr(paste0("^", after_base, "+"), after), "match.length")
      after_tag <- if (after_run >= 3 && after_base %in% alleles) paste0(after_base, "+", after_base, "\u00d7", after_run) else ""
      return(c(context = sprintf("%s[%s/%s]%s", left, alleles[1], alleles[2], right),
               homopolymer = trimws(paste(before_tag, after_tag))))
    }
  }
  c(context = "primer not found", homopolymer = "")
}

margin_context_values <- t(mapply(margin_context_f, margin_panel$locus, margin_panel$asp1, margin_panel$asp2)) 
margin_context <- tibble(locus = margin_panel$locus, context = margin_context_values[, "context"], homopolymer = margin_context_values[, "homopolymer"])

margin_display <- margin_display %>%
  left_join(margin_context, by = "locus") %>%
  mutate(locus_short = sub("_rs[0-9]+$", "", locus),
         homopolymer = ifelse(flagged, coalesce(homopolymer, ""), ""),
         axis_label = sprintf(paste0("%-", max(nchar(locus_short)), "s  %s  %s"), locus_short, context, homopolymer))
margin_name_width <- max(nchar(margin_display$locus_short))

margin_axis <- bind_rows(select(margin_display, y, axis_label), # vertical dots for the empty row
                         if (margin_has_break) tibble(y = min(filter(margin_display, line_part %in% "first")$y) - 1,
                                                      axis_label = paste(rep(sprintf(paste0("%-", margin_name_width, "s  %s"), ".", "."), 3),
                                                                         collapse = "\n")))

# the break: the line stops a bit above and below the empty row, each end with a short perpendicular tick
margin_line_data <- filter(margin_display, !flagged)
if (margin_has_break) {
  margin_break_from <- filter(margin_line_data, line_part == "first") %>% slice_tail(n = 1)
  margin_break_to <- filter(margin_line_data, line_part == "last") %>% slice_head(n = 1)
  margin_break <- tibble(y = margin_break_from$y - c(0.65, 1.35)) %>% 
    mutate(x = margin_break_from$frac_near_zero_margin_locus +
             (margin_break_to$frac_near_zero_margin_locus - margin_break_from$frac_near_zero_margin_locus) * (margin_break_from$y - y) / 2)
  margin_line_data <- bind_rows(margin_line_data,
                                tibble(y = margin_break$y, frac_near_zero_margin_locus = margin_break$x, line_part = c("first", "last")))
  margin_break_tick <- 0.012 * max(margin_locus_summary$frac_near_zero_margin_locus) 
}

 # up to the first break past the longest bar, no grid lines further right in the empty space
margin_x_breaks_f <- function(limits) { b <- breaks_pretty()(limits); b[b <= min(b[b >= max(margin_locus_summary$frac_near_zero_margin_locus)])] }

# Plot
# the two dashed lines, explained in the legend at the top instead of labels in the panel
margin_reference_lines <- tibble(x = c(margin_frac_under_cutoff, margin_outlier_threshold),

                                          sprintf("Outlier threshold, Q3 + 1.5 \u00d7 IQR (%.1f%%)", 100 * margin_outlier_threshold)))

p_near_zero_margin_by_locus <- ggplot() +

             size = 3, colour = "grey20", fill = "white", linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(1, "pt")) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = error_colour, `FALSE` = "grey60"), guide = "none") + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c("grey25", "#D99A1E"), margin_reference_lines$line), breaks = margin_reference_lines$line, name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(c("dashed", "dotted"), margin_reference_lines$line), breaks = margin_reference_lines$line, name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 0.6), theme = theme(legend.key.width = unit(22, "pt")))) +

  scale_y_continuous(breaks = margin_axis$y, labels = margin_axis$axis_label, expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 0.35))) + 
  labs(title = "Reads with no allele signal per locus",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d of %d loci above the outlier threshold, highest: %s (%.1f\u00d7 the average)",
                          length(margin_flagged_loci), nrow(margin_locus_summary), sub("_rs[0-9]+$", "", margin_worst_locus$locus),
                          margin_worst_locus$frac_near_zero_margin_locus / margin_frac_under_cutoff),
       x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = sprintf("Reads with no allele signal (score margin < %g)", margin_cutoff)) + 
  theme_minimal(base_family = plot_font, base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey30"),
        plot.title.position = "plot", # title and subtitle centred on the whole plot
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11, colour = "black", margin = margin(t = 6)),
        plot.caption.position = "plot",
        legend.position = "top",
        legend.location = "plot", # centred on the whole plot, like the title
        legend.text = element_text(size = 9.5, margin = margin(l = 5)), # same gap between every key and its label
        legend.key.spacing.x = unit(18, "pt"),
        legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), # even space above and below the legend: only the subtitle margin and legend.box.spacing
        legend.box.spacing = unit(6, "pt"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(family = "mono", size = 8.5, hjust = 0, colour = "black", lineheight = 0.55), 
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

print(p_near_zero_margin_by_locus)
margin_locus_plot_height <- 0.3 * margin_n_rows + 2.5
ggsave(file.path(qd_asp_dir, "near_zero_margin_by_locus.png"), p_near_zero_margin_by_locus, width = 12, height = margin_locus_plot_height, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(qd_asp_dir, "near_zero_margin_by_locus.pdf"), p_near_zero_margin_by_locus, width = 12, height = margin_locus_plot_height, device = cairo_pdf)


### Margin Plot: A = margin per read, B = close-up of the near-zero margins
margin_zoom_xmax <- 0.02 
margin_zoom_counts <- margin_plot_data %>%
  filter(panel == margin_panel_names[2], evidence <= margin_zoom_xmax) %>%

p_margin_panel_a <- p_score_margin_by_pass +

p_margin_panel_b <- p_near_zero_margin_by_locus +

p_margin_figure <- wrap_plots(free(p_margin_panel_a), p_margin_panel_b, ncol = 1, heights = c(1.5, 1)) +

# Zoom lines from the B box in panel A and the frame around panel B drawn on top
```

## Fisher strand analysis from GATK 
This chunk contains data prep and plots for strand bias analysis. It uses some ideas and indexes for rating strand bias from GATK such as Fisher Strand (FS) and the SOR index. It takes every read per locus and sample pair, creates a 2x2 table for two called alleles (minor/major rows (ab), fwd/rv (cd) columns) then the Fishers test asks if the FWD and RV ratio is the same for both alleles.
In HT you can expect the split to be reasonably equal, obviously some exemptions exist, but nothing outlandish. On the other hand, HM minor alleles which could also be called just "error reads" or "noise" often do come only from one strand. If one strand is heavily prefered for those error reads it can be a cause of a specific artifact (secondary structure, bias in pore loading, allele strand association, some weird alignment hopping, maybe even GC content and so on). This test specifically checks for those strand specific miscalls, FS is very dependent on depth, which plays a huge role obviously, the more reads a pair has the more confident FS index can be (usual cutoff value is > 60). p value is Phred scaled, the same as GATK FS = -10*log10(p), high FS means its very unlikely the split happened by chance. SOR (flags >3) index on the other hand is not that depended and strict with depth and is used in conjunction with FS.

Second plot shows strand bias of minor allele reads in HM in even more detail for all HM with depth >10 (necessary for statistics). Question guiding this second plot is whether the strand bias belongs to the loci (primers and sequence property) or the samples (library prep - in theory)? It plots a dumbbell graph showing all % of the minor allele reads by direction for every sample and locus, with bigger dots showing pooled minor allele readsper strand. It shows specific loci are more prone to FWD and other loci to the RV strand. It uses the same 2x2 table, error rate per strand is calculated as a/(a+b) on FWD, c/(c+d) on RV and odds ratio is calculated as OR = (a/b)/(c/d), if OR = 1 that means errors are on both strand equally often, if OR = 15 it means odd for an error are 15x more likely on a FWD strand. When minor reads or errors are rare this OR value is almost the same as the ratio of the two error alleles Its also symetric on a log scale for FWD and RV, it shows bias the same way regardless of % of error. Because some read have zero minor reads on some strand, I use a Haldane correction (+0.5), which would otherwise give 0 or infinity in OR, its used in panel B and Woolfs test. Mantel-Haenszel: OR is calcualted for once per locus from many different samples, its pooled from about 20 -25 HM pairs (depth >10). Samples count more the deeper they are, deeper samples have more weight. Result  is one pooled OR per locus with 95 % confidence interval (CI). One problem that can occur is, if you mix minor allele reads from one sample with another, thats why each sample is first compared with itself: one noisy sample with a lot of FWD reads (90/900) and RV (10/100) gives 10 % error rate on both (OR = 1) and one clean sample with FWD (1/100) AND rv (9/900) gives 1 % error rate on both (OR = 1). Mixing those two would give FWD 9.1% error rate  and RV 1.9% error rate, which makes the strand bias around 5 times more likely for FWD reads. This fake bias is called Simpsons paradox, we want to avoid this.
Solution: MH first calculates a*d/n (for FWD) and b*c/n (for RV), then it sums them up over samples OR_MH = Σ(a·d/n)/Σ(b·c/n) (errors between each sample never combine). Its also robust to 0 error reads so it doesnt need a +0.5 correction. CMH (Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel) give a p-value  per locus for null hypothesis that pooled OR = 1 with Bonferroni correction (divides threshold by the number of tests 0.05/33) - those loci which survive have coloured test results in the middle plot column.
If deep samples carry more weight this also means that one single deep read can overpower a sample. Woolfs test tests exactly for that. At each locus it takes each sample log OR (with correction), computes a weighted mean (samples with more read count more) and it measures how far samples disperse around the mean as chisquare statistic. If they scatter no more than random noise the samples agree. Results show samples comply at every locus, bias comes from the locus and not the sample.

For just described methods one assumption must hold, its that all reads or every data point is independent, which in the case of amplicon it is not (PCR can reproduce same error, different multiplication rate for different reads and so on). It can make the evidence feel too confident and p values very small. GLMM check for that.

```{r GATK_Fisher_Strand_Analysis, eval = params$run_filtration_parameters, fig.width = 11.69, fig.height = 8.27, out.width = "100%"}
# This chunk contains FS per pair, allelef frequency by strand with SOR and FS, strand odds ratio of HM minor allele reads and GLMM that checks the odds ratio results.
# Output folder for Fisher strand analysis
out_dir_FS <- file.path(graphics_dir, "Genotype_Filtration_Parameters/Fisher_strand_analysis")
dir.create(out_dir_FS, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Reads form the ASP run with direction column
strand_reads <- read_tsv(asp_reads_path, col_select = c(barcode, locus, direction, called_allele),
                         col_types = cols(barcode = "c", locus = "c", direction = "c", called_allele = "c"))

# Call status and zygosity of every called read, built the same way as earlier chunks
fs_calls <- asp_results %>%
  filter(status == "called") %>%
  transmute(sample = barcode, locus, genotype) %>%
  mutate(zygosity_call = ifelse(substr(genotype, 1, 1) == substr(genotype, 2, 2), "Homozygous", "Heterozygous")) %>%
  left_join(ref %>% select(sample, locus, reference_genotype = genotype), by = c("sample", "locus")) %>%
  mutate(call_status = case_when(is.na(reference_genotype) ~ "No reference",
                                 genotype == reference_genotype ~ "Correct",
                                 TRUE ~ "Miscalled"))

# Two alleles of every locus from the primer panel the genotyping pipeline used
fs_panel_alleles <- select(panel, locus, allele1, allele2)

# GATK hard filter, everything above FS > 60 is marked as biased
fs_gatk_cutoff <- 60 
fs_zygosity_fills <- c(Homozygous = hm_dark, Heterozygous = ht_dark)

# GATK per locus and smaple pair style analysis. It takes all reads of one pair and returns the Fisher Strand score (FS), p-value and number of alleles.
fs_compute <- function(df) {
  tbl <- df %>%
    count(called_allele, direction) %>% # Counts alleles per direction
    pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) # Turns direction into columns

  # Checks if both alleles and directions are present otherwise it can't work, returns number of alleles
  if (nrow(tbl) < 2 || !all(c("forward", "reverse") %in% names(tbl))) {
    return(tibble(fs = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_, n_alleles = nrow(tbl)))
  }

  # Takes two count columns and makes a 2x2 grid and checks how likely that strand split is
  p <- fisher.test(as.matrix(tbl[, c("forward", "reverse")]))$p.value
  # Converts it to FS, it uses the same Phred scale as base quality (smaller p meand bigger FS). 
  tibble(fs = round(-10 * log10(p), 2), p_value = p, n_alleles = nrow(tbl))
}

# This part runs previous function n every locus sample pair and collect the results. Results contain function returns and whether the genotype call was correct.
fs_by_pair <- strand_reads %>%
  filter(!is.na(called_allele)) %>%
  group_by(sample = barcode, locus) %>%
  group_modify(~ fs_compute(.x)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(fs_calls %>% select(sample, locus, call_status, zygosity_call), by = c("sample", "locus")) # adds call status and zygosity

# This part calculates lowest number of reads needed to pass the FS > 60 cutoff. It tests the most biased 2x2 matrix, below those number of reads, strands can still be biased but there is just not enough evidence to call them out.
fs_read_counts_test <- 2:200
fs_max_possible <- -10 * log10(2 / choose(fs_read_counts_test, floor(fs_read_counts_test / 2)))
fs_min_reads_for_cutoff_test <- min(fs_read_counts_test[fs_max_possible > fs_gatk_cutoff])
cat(sprintf("FS can only exceed %d with at least %d reads.\n", fs_gatk_cutoff, fs_min_reads_for_cutoff_test))

# Makes a table of miscalls only with their FS results, arranged from highest to lowest
fs_miscalled <- fs_by_pair %>%
  filter(call_status == "Miscalled") %>%
  arrange(desc(fs))
kable(fs_miscalled, col.names = c("Sample", "Locus", "FS", "p", "Alleles", "Call", "Zygosity"))

### Can i use FS as a predictor for miscalls (checked on all locus and sample pairs)?

# Creates a table of pairs for the plot, pairs where FS can be calculated and had a genotype call and adds a Benjamini-Hochberg correction (comparing many pairs at once, at 5 % a lot of pairs become significant by pure chance)
fs_all_pairs <- fs_by_pair %>%
  filter(!is.na(fs), !is.na(zygosity_call)) %>% 
  mutate(fs_padj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")) 

# One point per genotype call coloured by zygosity. High FS for HM (minor allele reads come from one strand only), HT are balanced as expected
p_fs_by_zygosity <- ggplot(fs_all_pairs, aes(x = fs, y = zygosity_call, colour = zygosity_call)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = fs_gatk_cutoff, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.15, width = 0, alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = fs_zygosity_fills, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Fisher Strand per called genotype: HM vs HT",
       subtitle = sprintf("One point per genotype with reads for both alleles - dashed line = GATK's FS = %d cutoff.\nHigh FS: minor allele reads in a HM call come from one strand. FS can only exceed %d with at least %d reads.", fs_gatk_cutoff, fs_gatk_cutoff, fs_min_reads_for_cutoff_test),
       x = "FS (phred-scaled Fisher's exact test)", 
       y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = plot_font, base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

print(p_fs_by_zygosity)
ggsave(file.path(out_dir_FS, "fisher_strand_by_zygosity.png"), p_fs_by_zygosity, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(out_dir_FS, "fisher_strand_by_zygosity.pdf"), p_fs_by_zygosity, width = 9, height = 5, device = cairo_pdf)

# Summary stats of FS results
fs_summary <- fs_all_pairs %>%
  group_by(zygosity_call, call_status) %>%
  summarise(n_pairs = n(),
            pct_fs_over_60 = round(100 * mean(fs > fs_gatk_cutoff), 1), # % of pairs GATK would flag
            median_fs = round(median(fs), 1),
            n_significant_after_BH = sum(fs_padj < 0.05), # number of signicant pairs after BH correction
            .groups = "drop")
kable(fs_summary, col.names = c("Zygosity", "Call", "Pairs", "FS > 60 (%)", "Median FS", "Significant after BH"))

# Allele and strand read count for every miscall, prints them out
fs_miscall_reads <- strand_reads %>%
  filter(!is.na(called_allele)) %>%
  semi_join(filter(fs_calls, call_status == "Miscalled") %>% select(barcode = sample, locus), by = c("barcode", "locus")) %>%
  count(barcode, locus, called_allele, direction) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
kable(fs_miscall_reads, col.names = c("Sample", "Locus", "Allele", "Forward reads", "Reverse reads"))

### 2. Plot, big panel and data prep (strand bias panel)

sb_min_reads_per_strand <- 10 # cutoff for depth
   sb_allele_colours <- c("HT major" = ht_dark, "HT minor" = ht_light, "HM major" = hm_dark, "HM minor" = hm_light)
sb_zoom_max <- 10 # to which % it zooms in on the panel
sb_fs_colour_max <- 100 # FS colour scale, sets a cap so points after this number get the darkerst colour (seperation is more visibile)
sb_sor_colour_max <- 4 # SOR colour scale
sb_sor_cutoff <- 3 # SOR cutoff, recommended by GATK

# Table of both alleles for very locus, one per row
sb_locus_alleles <- fs_panel_alleles %>%
  pivot_longer(c(allele1, allele2), values_to = "called_allele") %>%
  select(locus, called_allele)

# Counts voting reads per pair, allele and strand for called reads
sb_counts <- strand_reads %>%
  filter(!is.na(called_allele)) %>%
  semi_join(fs_calls %>% select(barcode = sample, locus), by = c("barcode", "locus")) %>%
  count(barcode, locus, called_allele, direction)

# reads per allele and strand for every called genotype with FWD and RV columns
sb_counts_wide <- sb_counts %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  rename(n_fwd = forward, n_rev = reverse)

# Build a table for both alleles for every pair, 0 reads when an allele has none, each share of the the FWD and RV reads, and which is the major one
sb_allele_strand <- sb_counts %>%
  distinct(barcode, locus) %>%
  inner_join(sb_locus_alleles, by = "locus", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  left_join(sb_counts_wide, by = c("barcode", "locus", "called_allele")) %>%
  mutate(n_fwd = coalesce(n_fwd, 0L), n_rev = coalesce(n_rev, 0L)) %>%
  arrange(barcode, locus, called_allele) %>%
  group_by(barcode, locus) %>%
  filter(sum(n_fwd) >= sb_min_reads_per_strand, sum(n_rev) >= sb_min_reads_per_strand) %>%
  mutate(pct_fwd = 100 * n_fwd / sum(n_fwd),
         pct_rev = 100 * n_rev / sum(n_rev),
         reads = n_fwd + n_rev,
         allele_role = ifelse(row_number(desc(reads)) == 1, "Major", "Minor")) %>% 
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(fs_calls %>% select(barcode = sample, locus, zygosity_call), by = c("barcode", "locus")) %>%
  mutate(allele_group = factor(paste(ifelse(zygosity_call == "Heterozygous", "HT", "HM"), tolower(allele_role)), levels = names(sb_allele_colours)))

# Prepares the data fro the titles and the main title.
sb_n_pairs_called <- n_distinct(paste(sb_counts$barcode, sb_counts$locus))
sb_n_pairs_shown <- n_distinct(paste(sb_allele_strand$barcode, sb_allele_strand$locus))
sb_main_title <- sprintf("Called genotypes with \u2265 %d voting reads on each strand: %d of %d pairs", # \u2265 is the >= symbol
                         sb_min_reads_per_strand, sb_n_pairs_shown, sb_n_pairs_called)

# FS from every pairs calculated previously, pairs reads only for one allele got NA, so now thats FS = 0
sb_pair_fs <- sb_allele_strand %>%
  distinct(barcode, locus) %>%
  left_join(fs_by_pair %>% select(barcode = sample, locus, fs), by = c("barcode", "locus")) %>%
  mutate(fs = coalesce(fs, 0)) # NA becomes 0

# This part calucaltes SOR (GATK) for every pair from the same 2x2 table with 1 read added to every cell (major = ref, minor = alt):
# SOR = ln(R + 1/R) + ln(min(major_fwd, major_rev) / max(major_fwd, major_rev)) - ln(min(minor_fwd, minor_rev) / max(minor_fwd, minor_rev)),
# R = (major_fwd / major_rev) / (minor_fwd / minor_rev), the odds ratio
sb_pair_sor <- sb_allele_strand %>%
  group_by(barcode, locus) %>%
  summarise(major_fwd = n_fwd[allele_role == "Major"] + 1, major_rev = n_rev[allele_role == "Major"] + 1,
            minor_fwd = n_fwd[allele_role == "Minor"] + 1, minor_rev = n_rev[allele_role == "Minor"] + 1, .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(r = (major_fwd / major_rev) / (minor_fwd / minor_rev),
         sor = log(r + 1 / r) + log(pmin(major_fwd, major_rev) / pmax(major_fwd, major_rev)) - log(pmin(minor_fwd, minor_rev) / pmax(minor_fwd, minor_rev))) %>%
  select(barcode, locus, sor)

# Count how many pairs the SOR filter would remove and prints the report
sb_n_fs_over <- sum(sb_pair_fs$fs > fs_gatk_cutoff)
sb_n_sor_over <- sum(sb_pair_sor$sor > sb_sor_cutoff)
cat(sprintf("FS > %d: %d of %d pairs; SOR > %g: %d of %d pairs\n", fs_gatk_cutoff, sb_n_fs_over, nrow(sb_pair_fs), sb_sor_cutoff, sb_n_sor_over, nrow(sb_pair_sor)))

# Prepares data for the zoomed panel which shows minor alleles on fwd and rv strands coloured by SOR or FS index value
sb_minor_zoom <- sb_allele_strand %>%
  filter(allele_role == "Minor", pct_fwd <= sb_zoom_max, pct_rev <= sb_zoom_max) %>% # filters for under 10 %
  left_join(sb_pair_fs, by = c("barcode", "locus")) %>%
  left_join(sb_pair_sor, by = c("barcode", "locus"))
cat(sprintf("zoomed panel: %d of %d minor alleles (the rest are heterozygote alleles or above %d%%)\n",
            nrow(sb_minor_zoom), sum(sb_allele_strand$allele_role == "Minor"), sb_zoom_max))

# Black square around the botto panels
sb_square <- c(low = -1, high = sb_zoom_max + 1)
sb_line_colour <- "grey55" # Zoom line for the C and D frame
sb_theme <- theme_minimal(base_family = plot_font, base_size = 12) + 
            theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
                  plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")) 

# Plot A: all alleles with a black square showing zoomed area
p_sb_allele_all <- ggplot(sb_allele_strand, aes(x = pct_fwd, y = pct_rev, colour = allele_group)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.6) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = sb_square[["low"]], xmax = sb_square[["high"]], ymin = sb_square[["low"]], ymax = sb_square[["high"]],
           fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  annotate("curve", x = 62, y = 24, xend = 39, yend = 39, curvature = -0.3, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5,
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), type = "closed")) + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), labels = label_percent(scale = 1), position = "top", name = "Share of FORWARD reads") +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), labels = label_percent(scale = 1), name = "Share of REVERSE reads") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = sb_allele_colours, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
  annotate("text", x = 58, y = 20, hjust = 0, size = 3.4, colour = "grey30", lineheight = 0.95,
           label = "dashed diagonal = allele read\nequally often from both strands") +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 100), clip = "off") + # limits here (not in the scales) so the square is not cut off
  labs(title = "A  All alleles: forward vs reverse strand") +
  sb_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "none") # Shared legend next to panel B

# Data prep for Plot B, where x axis is allele frequency, the mean of its share among fwd and rv reads in log scale and y axis is strand asymmetry (fwd - rev) / (fwd + rev), where 1 = only FWD reads, -1 = only RV reads, 0 = balanced. This calculates both values for panel B.
sb_asym_data <- sb_allele_strand %>%
  mutate(allele_freq = (pct_fwd + pct_rev) / 2,
         asymmetry = ifelse(pct_fwd + pct_rev > 0, (pct_fwd - pct_rev) / (pct_fwd + pct_rev), 0))

# Minor allele reads on only one strand
sb_asym_one_strand <- sb_asym_data %>%

### Strand bias of the minor allele reads in HM calls with more than 10 reads measured as an odds ratio. For every sample the same 2x2 matrix is created and odds ratio calculated as (OR) = (minor/major on FWD)/(minor/major on RV), if its > 1 than minor allele is more on FWD and < 1 more on RV. Per locus sample tables are combined with Mantel-Haenszel method (sample weighted by its depth) and Woolffs test to check if the if OR differs between samples or loci.

sbo_fwd_colour <- fwd_colour # FWD minor allele
sbo_rev_colour <- rv_colour # RV minor allele
sbo_axis_rv <- 10 # Panel A x axis RV max (%)
sbo_axis_fwd <- 15 # Panel A x axis FWD max (%)

# Minor and major allele for both strands, error rate and the log2 odds ratio with the Haldanes correction (+ 0.5), setup for the 2x2 matrix
sbo_hm_pairs_all <- sb_allele_strand %>%
  filter(zygosity_call == "Homozygous") %>%
  group_by(barcode, locus) %>%
  summarise(minor_fwd = n_fwd[allele_role == "Minor"], major_fwd = n_fwd[allele_role == "Major"],
            minor_rev = n_rev[allele_role == "Minor"], major_rev = n_rev[allele_role == "Major"],
            rate_fwd = pct_fwd[allele_role == "Minor"], rate_rev = pct_rev[allele_role == "Minor"], .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(log2_or = log2(((minor_fwd + 0.5) * (major_rev + 0.5)) / ((major_fwd + 0.5) * (minor_rev + 0.5))))

# Loci needs atleast 2 HM samples to be able to run the mantelhaen.test (one samle cant show agreement or variation)
sbo_skipped <- sbo_hm_pairs_all %>%
  group_by(locus) %>%
  summarise(samples = n(), minor_reads = sum(minor_fwd + minor_rev), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(samples < 2 | minor_reads == 0) # Filters for loci with zero minor reads or less than two HM samples
if (nrow(sbo_skipped) > 0) {
  cat("Loci left out of the odds-ratio figure (fewer than 2 HM samples or no minor allele reads):\n")
  print(kable(sbo_skipped))
}
sbo_hm_pairs <- anti_join(sbo_hm_pairs_all, sbo_skipped, by = "locus") # Removes loci which are on the skipped list

# Woolf's test: do all samples show the same strand bias at the same loci or not (chi-square of the per-sample log ORs around their weighted mean)
sbo_woolf_p <- function(minor_fwd, major_fwd, minor_rev, major_rev) {
  log_or <- log(((minor_fwd + 0.5) * (major_rev + 0.5)) / ((major_fwd + 0.5) * (minor_rev + 0.5)))
  weight <- 1 / (1 / (minor_fwd + 0.5) + 1 / (major_fwd + 0.5) + 1 / (minor_rev + 0.5) + 1 / (major_rev + 0.5))
  chi2 <- sum(weight * (log_or - sum(weight * log_or) / sum(weight))^2)
  pchisq(chi2, df = length(log_or) - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
}

# Mantel-Haenszel test over the samples of one locus (one 2x2 table per sample) and pooled OR with 95 % CI and the CMH p-value
sbo_mh <- function(minor_fwd, minor_rev, major_fwd, major_rev) {
  mh <- mantelhaen.test(array(rbind(minor_fwd, minor_rev, major_fwd, major_rev), dim = c(2, 2, length(minor_fwd))), exact = FALSE)
  tibble(or = unname(mh$estimate), or_low = mh$conf.int[1], or_high = mh$conf.int[2], p = mh$p.value)
}

sbo_loci <- sbo_hm_pairs %>%
  group_by(locus) %>%
  summarise(samples = n(),
            sbo_mh(minor_fwd, minor_rev, major_fwd, major_rev),
            homogeneity_p = sbo_woolf_p(minor_fwd, major_fwd, minor_rev, major_rev),
            rate_fwd = 100 * sum(minor_fwd) / sum(minor_fwd + major_fwd),
            rate_rev = 100 * sum(minor_rev) / sum(minor_rev + major_rev)) %>%
  arrange(or) %>%
  mutate(locus = factor(locus, levels = locus),
         significant = p < 0.05 / n(), # CMH test, Bonferroni over all loci
         or_label = ifelse(or >= 1, sprintf("%.1fx FWD (%.1f-%.1f)", or, or_low, or_high),
                           sprintf("%.1fx RV (%.1f-%.1f)", 1 / or, 1 / or_high, 1 / or_low)),
         label_colour = case_when(!significant ~ "ns", or >= 1 ~ "FWD", TRUE ~ "RV")) # grey = not significant
write_tsv(sbo_loci, file.path(out_dir_FS, "strand_bias_by_locus.tsv")) 

sbo_hm_pairs_ordered <- mutate(sbo_hm_pairs, locus = factor(locus, levels = levels(sbo_loci$locus))) # same locus order as the figure
kable(select(sbo_loci, locus, samples, or, or_low, or_high, p, homogeneity_p), digits = 3,
      col.names = c("Locus", "HM samples", "Pooled OR (MH)", "95 % CI low", "95 % CI high", "CMH p", "Woolf p"))

cat(sprintf("bias significant (p < 0.05) at %d of %d loci, %d after Bonferroni; OR differs between samples (Woolf p < 0.05) at %d loci (smallest p = %.2f)\n",
            sum(sbo_loci$p < 0.05), nrow(sbo_loci), sum(sbo_loci$significant), sum(sbo_loci$homogeneity_p < 0.05), min(sbo_loci$homogeneity_p)))

# Plot A: minor allele rate per strand
sbo_points <- sbo_hm_pairs_ordered %>% # one point per sample and strand
  select(barcode, locus, rate_fwd, rate_rev) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(rate_fwd, rate_rev), names_to = "strand", values_to = "rate") %>%
  mutate(strand = ifelse(strand == "rate_fwd", "FWD", "RV"),
         x = ifelse(strand == "RV", -rate, rate),
         beyond = x < -sbo_axis_rv | x > sbo_axis_fwd,
         x = pmin(pmax(x, -sbo_axis_rv), sbo_axis_fwd))

p_sbo_rates <- ggplot(sbo_loci, aes(y = locus)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey55") +
  geom_point(data = filter(sbo_points, !beyond), aes(x = x, colour = strand), alpha = 0.5, size = 1.2,
             position = position_jitter(height = 0.15, width = 0, seed = 1)) +
  geom_point(data = filter(sbo_points, beyond), aes(x = x, colour = strand), shape = 2, size = 1.8) + 
  geom_segment(aes(x = -rate_rev, xend = rate_fwd, yend = locus), colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(x = -rate_rev), shape = 21, size = 3.2, fill = sbo_rev_colour, colour = "white", stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(x = rate_fwd), shape = 21, size = 3.2, fill = sbo_fwd_colour, colour = "white", stroke = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(x = sbo_axis_fwd + 1, label = or_label, colour = label_colour), hjust = 0, size = 3.1) + # locus OR (95 % CI)
  annotate("text", x = sbo_axis_fwd + 1, y = nrow(sbo_loci) + 0.75, label = "Odds ratio (95% CI)", hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = 3.1, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(FWD = sbo_fwd_colour, RV = sbo_rev_colour, ns = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-sbo_axis_rv, sbo_axis_fwd, 5), labels = function(x) paste0(abs(x), "%")) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-sbo_axis_rv, sbo_axis_fwd), ylim = c(1, nrow(sbo_loci)), clip = "off") +
  labs(title = "A  Minor allele rate on reverse and forward reads",
       subtitle = sprintf("Small points represent the %% of minor allele reads on the FWD (red) and RV (blue) strand of one sample,\nlarge points all HM reads pooled per locus. Right: Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio (95%% CI) of minor allele reads on FWD vs RV;\ncoloured = strand bias significant after Bonferroni (CMH p < 0.05/%d: %d of %d loci), grey = not significant.",
                          nrow(sbo_loci), sum(sbo_loci$significant), nrow(sbo_loci)),
       x = "% of minor allele reads per strand", y = NULL) +
  sb_theme +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(5.5, 120, 5.5, 5.5)) 

# Plot B: each sample's OR, one line per sample down the loci on a log2 scale, each line connect the loci
sbo_line_steps <- sbo_hm_pairs_ordered %>%
  mutate(y = as.integer(locus)) %>%
  arrange(barcode, y) %>%
  group_by(barcode) %>%
  mutate(x_end = lead(log2_or), y_end = lead(y)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(x_end)) %>%
  transmute(barcode, x = log2_or, y, x_end, y_end,
            y_cross = ifelse(sign(x) != sign(x_end) & x != 0 & x_end != 0, y + (y_end - y) * x / (x - x_end), NA_real_)) # where it crosses OR = 1

sbo_line_segments <- bind_rows(
  filter(sbo_line_steps, is.na(y_cross)) %>% select(barcode, x, y, x_end, y_end), # segments on one side of OR = 1
  filter(sbo_line_steps, !is.na(y_cross)) %>% transmute(barcode, x, y, x_end = 0, y_end = y_cross), # crossing: first part
  filter(sbo_line_steps, !is.na(y_cross)) %>% transmute(barcode, x = 0, y = y_cross, x_end, y_end)) %>% # crossing: second part
  mutate(side = ifelse(x + x_end >= 0, "FWD", "RV"))

sbo_or_breaks <- seq(-6, 6, 2) # log2 OR: 1x, 4x, 16x, 64x more on either strand

p_sbo_lines <- ggplot(sbo_line_segments) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = x, xend = x_end, y = y, yend = y_end, colour = side), alpha = 0.6, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_path(data = arrange(sbo_loci, locus), aes(x = log2(or), y = as.integer(locus)), colour = "black", linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(FWD = sbo_fwd_colour, RV = sbo_rev_colour), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sbo_or_breaks, labels = function(x) paste0(2^abs(x), "x")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_len(nrow(sbo_loci)), labels = NULL, expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(1, nrow(sbo_loci))) + 
  labs(title = "B  Minor allele strand odds ratio per sample",
       subtitle = sprintf("One line per sample (OR with +0.5 Haldane correction;\nred = more on FWD, blue = more on RV), black line = Mantel-Haenszel OR of all samples.\nWoolf test: samples differ at %d of %d loci (smallest p = %.2f).",
                          sum(sbo_loci$homogeneity_p < 0.05), nrow(sbo_loci), min(sbo_loci$homogeneity_p)),
       x = "OR (log scale)", y = NULL) +
  sb_theme +
  theme(panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank())

### GLMM, mixed model for the strand bias on minor allele reads in hM pairs with more than 10 reads. MH and Woolf treat reads as independent pieces of evidence, that is not true with PCR and earlier errors that can happen during this step (pcr copies of one molecule, strnad bias amplification). So the p values can be a bit optimistic. Each pair becomes two rows FWD and RV, minor reads out of all reads on that strand.
# strand_c: +0.5 = forward, -0.5 = reverse, so its coefficient is the log OR forward vs reverse.

sbm_data <- sbo_hm_pairs %>%
  select(barcode, locus, minor_fwd, major_fwd, minor_rev, major_rev) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(barcode, locus), names_to = c(".value", "strand"), names_sep = "_") %>% # columns minor, major; strand = fwd / rev
  mutate(strand_c = ifelse(strand == "fwd", 0.5, -0.5), # intercept is halfway between the strands
         obs = factor(row_number())) 

# full model: every locus and every sample gets its own error level and its own strand bias (1 + strand_c || ...),
# (1 | obs) gives every row its own extra noise, which absorbs the PCR copies (reads not independent)
# a "singular fit" message means a variance is estimated as 0 - that is a result, not an error
sbm_full <- glmer(cbind(minor, major) ~ strand_c + (1 + strand_c || locus) + (1 + strand_c || barcode) + (1 | obs),
                  data = sbm_data, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

# the same model, but all loci share one strand bias
sbm_no_locus_bias <- glmer(cbind(minor, major) ~ strand_c + (1 | locus) + (1 + strand_c || barcode) + (1 | obs),
                           data = sbm_data, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

# the same model, but all samples share one strand bias
sbm_no_sample_bias <- glmer(cbind(minor, major) ~ strand_c + (1 + strand_c || locus) + (1 | barcode) + (1 | obs),
                            data = sbm_data, family = binomial, control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

# how much the strand bias (log OR) varies between loci and between samples (standard deviations)
sbm_bias_sd <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(sbm_full)) %>% filter(var1 == "strand_c")
sbm_bias_sd_locus <- sbm_bias_sd$sdcor[startsWith(sbm_bias_sd$grp, "locus")]
sbm_bias_sd_sample <- sbm_bias_sd$sdcor[startsWith(sbm_bias_sd$grp, "barcode")]

# likelihood ratio tests: does the model get worse without that variation? p is halved because a variance cannot be below 0
sbm_p_locus <- anova(sbm_no_locus_bias, sbm_full)$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2] / 2
sbm_p_sample <- anova(sbm_no_sample_bias, sbm_full)$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2] / 2
cat(sprintf("Strand bias SD between loci: %.2f (p = %.2g), between samples: %.2f (p = %.2g)\n",
            sbm_bias_sd_locus, sbm_p_locus, sbm_bias_sd_sample, sbm_p_sample))

# The odds-ratio figure (A + B) with the findings of all three analyses as its caption
sbo_findings <- sprintf("CMH: strand bias significant at %d of %d loci after Bonferroni. Woolf: samples differ at %d of %d loci.\nGLMM (reads not independent): strand-bias SD between loci %.2f (p = %.2g) vs between samples %.2f (p = %.2g).",
                        sum(sbo_loci$significant), nrow(sbo_loci), sum(sbo_loci$homogeneity_p < 0.05), nrow(sbo_loci),
                        sbm_bias_sd_locus, sbm_p_locus, sbm_bias_sd_sample, sbm_p_sample)

p_sbo_figure <- wrap_plots(p_sbo_rates, p_sbo_lines, widths = c(1.6, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(title = "The strand bias of the minor allele reads in HM pairs (depth \u2265 10) belongs to the locus",
                  caption = sbo_findings,
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
                                plot.caption = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0)))

sbo_figure_png <- file.path(out_dir_FS, "strand_bias_odds_ratio.png")
ggsave(sbo_figure_png, p_sbo_figure, width = 16, height = 10.8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(out_dir_FS, "strand_bias_odds_ratio.pdf"), p_sbo_figure, width = 16, height = 10.8, device = cairo_pdf)
include_graphics(normalizePath(sbo_figure_png), rel_path = FALSE)
```



## Amplicon rank analysis and visualization  
This chunk contains data prep and plots for amplicon rank analysis. Amplicons form longer ligated concatemers which are separated into sample specific .fastq files by first Dorado demultiplexing with STA and LSP primers. The actual amplicon rank is determined by ObiTools4 demultiplexing (for example 1/2, 2/2, 1/1, 4/9,...) which split the read into chunks of sequence (amplicon). Those amplicons are then used for SNP and allele calling with ASP1 and ASP2 primers.
Main idea behind this chunk is how the amplicon rank effects the quality and confidence for allele calling, it searches for pattern betwen amplicon position in a read and its allele calling success rate and SNP calling. How trusting are those ranks, can one really say a singleton is a singleton and not just a longer sequence of ligated amplicon which couldnt be assigned to a specific locus just by pure coincidence or because of higher number of mismatches allowed when aligning the primers. The amplicons are therefor checked for flanking sequences, where those are, how long are those sequence and divides it by median length of an ampicon (116). this gives an estimation of how many "amplicon" are left untouched. This is the idea behind adjusted concatemer of 6 found amplicon has a flanking sequences after first amplicon the ranks are adjusted (1 -> 1, 2 -> 3, 3 -> 4) and the whole concatemer is pushed to 6 -> 7.

It also plots some basic bar plots with patchworked pie plots showing number of amplicons by concatemer size and share of singletons and other panels of basic information.

```{r Amplicon_Rank_Size_and_Position, eval = params$run_filtration_parameters, fig.width = 8.27, fig.height = 5.5, out.width = "70%"}
stopifnot("run the setup chunk first" = exists("graphics_dir") && exists("asp_reads_path") && exists("dataset_name"),
          "run the FS chunk first (ref, fs_calls)" = exists("ref") && exists("fs_calls"),
          "run the QD chunk first (margin_fate_colours, margin_min_snp_quality)" = exists("margin_fate_colours") && exists("margin_min_snp_quality"))

# Output paths and editable variables
concat_out_dir <- file.path(graphics_dir, "Genotype_filtration_parameters/Amplicon_rank_analysis")
dir.create(concat_out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
concat_raw_fastq_dir <- sprintf("Data/Processed_data/%s/Demultiplexed_sequence_data/Dorado_demultiplexed_by_sample", dataset_name)
concat_identified_fastq_dir <- sprintf("Data/Processed_data/%s/Demultiplexed_sequence_data/Identified_sample_sequences_Obi4", dataset_name)
concat_barcodes <- sprintf("barcode%02d", seq_len(n_barcodes))
concat_largest_size_shown <- 15 # heatmap shows concatemers to this size
concat_pool_sizes_from <- 12 # in statistics, from those upwards are pooled, each on their won dont contain enough data
concat_min_amplicons <- 30 # heatmap tiles a regrey with fewer than this number of reads

# Colours for the plots
concat_brown <- "#8B775F"; concat_sage <- "#9AA582"; concat_dark_green <- "#657359"; concat_beige <- "#D7C9BE"; concat_cream <- "#F1E4DB"
concat_darken_f <- function(colours) setNames(rgb(t(col2rgb(colours) * 0.7), maxColorValue = 255), names(colours))
concat_theme <- theme_minimal(base_family = plot_font, base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
        plot.title.position = "plot",
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey30"),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# Data prep
concat_amplicons <- read_tsv(asp_reads_path, col_select = c(barcode, locus, read_id, amplicon_rank, called_allele, relative_margin,
                            snp_position_quality, tie_flag, below_threshold_flag, forward_error, reverse_error),
                            col_types = cols(.default = "c", relative_margin = "d", snp_position_quality = "i", tie_flag = "l",
                            below_threshold_flag = "l", forward_error = "i", reverse_error = "i"))

# Positions of each amplicons inside the read
concat_amplicons <- concat_amplicons %>%
  separate(amplicon_rank, into = c("concatemer_rank", "concatemer_size"), sep = "/", convert = TRUE) %>% # separates the ranks
  mutate(raw_read_id = sub("_sub\\[.*\\]$", "", read_id), # parent read
         read_type = ifelse(concatemer_size == 1, "Singleton", "In concatemer"),
         position_type = factor(case_when(concatemer_size == 1 ~ "Singleton",
                                          concatemer_rank == 1 ~ "First",
                                          concatemer_rank == concatemer_size ~ "Last",
                                          TRUE ~ "Middle"), levels = c("Singleton", "First", "Middle", "Last")))

# Table with reasons why the reads weren't used
concat_amplicons <- concat_amplicons %>%
  mutate(fate = factor(case_when(!is.na(called_allele) ~ "Used for genotyping",
                                 tie_flag ~ "No allele signal (tie)",
                                 below_threshold_flag ~ "Poor alignment",
                                 TRUE ~ "Failed a SNP check"), levels = names(margin_fate_colours)))

# Comparison with reference
concat_amplicons <- concat_amplicons %>%
  left_join(select(ref, barcode = sample, locus, reference_genotype = genotype), by = c("barcode", "locus")) %>%
  mutate(outcome = factor(case_when(is.na(reference_genotype) ~ NA_character_,
                                    is.na(called_allele) ~ "Failed to call",
                                    called_allele == substr(reference_genotype, 1, 1) | called_allele == substr(reference_genotype, 2, 2) ~ "Called - correct", TRUE ~ "Called - wrong"), levels = c("Failed to call", "Called - wrong", "Called - correct")))

concat_group_colours <- c(Singleton = concat_brown, "In concatemer" = concat_sage, 
                          First = concat_dark_green, Middle = concat_sage, Last = concat_beige)
concat_outcome_colours <- c("Failed to call" = concat_beige, "Called - wrong" = error_colour, "Called - correct" = correct_colour)

# 1. Plot,  concatemer size distribution with barplot and patchworked pie chart showing share of singletons
# Counts of amplicons per concatemer size
concat_amplicons_per_size <- count(concat_amplicons, concatemer_size, read_type, name = "n_amplicons")
concat_singleton_share <- concat_amplicons %>%
  count(read_type) %>%
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n))

kable(concat_amplicons_per_size)
```

```{r Amplicon_Rank_Per_Locus_Sample_and_Raw_Reads, eval = params$run_filtration_parameters, fig.width = 11.69, fig.height = 8.27, out.width = "100%"}
# 5. Plot, concatemer size per locus and per sample
concat_short_locus_name_f <- function(locus) sub("_rs[0-9]+$", "", locus) # Shortens longer names, too white space for example TIGRP2P116705_rs8955982

# function calculates what share of each locus or sample amplicon come different raw read sizes
concat_size_shares_f <- function(group_column) {
  concat_amplicons %>%
mutate(size_group = cut(concatemer_size, breaks = c(0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, Inf), labels = c("1", "2-3", "4-5", "6-7", "8-10", "11+")), # concatemers sizes
           group = .data[[group_column]]) %>%
    count(group, size_group) %>%
    group_by(group) %>%
    mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n), singleton_pct = sum(pct[size_group == "1"])) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(group = reorder(group, singleton_pct))
}
concat_size_shares_by_locus <- concat_size_shares_f("locus") %>%
  mutate(group = factor(concat_short_locus_name_f(as.character(group)), levels = concat_short_locus_name_f(levels(group))))
concat_size_shares_by_sample <- concat_size_shares_f("barcode")


concat_size_group_colours <- c("1" = concat_brown, "2-3" = "#D3D8C5", "4-5" = "#B4BC9F", "6-7" = concat_sage, "8-10" = concat_dark_green, "11+" = "#46503E")

p_concat_size_shares <- ggplot(concat_size_shares, aes(x = pct, y = group, fill = size_group, colour = size_group)) +

  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1), colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +

  labs(title = "Concatemer size of the ampliicons, per locus and per sample",
       subtitle = "Sorted by the share of singletons (brown), most at the top",
       x = "Share of amplicons", y = NULL) +
  concat_theme +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5), plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, hjust = 0), 
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "top")

# 7. Plot, raw reads vs the the amplicons found inside, are those really singletons or just longer reads with no matched primers?
# Reads fastq files, parses the reads from headers to sequence
concat_read_fastq_f <- function(path) { 
  fastq_lines <- readLines(path)
  list(header = fastq_lines[seq(1, length(fastq_lines), 4)], sequence = fastq_lines[seq(2, length(fastq_lines), 4)])
}
# Finds sample files
concat_find_file_f <- function(folder, pattern) {
  matches <- Sys.glob(file.path(folder, pattern))
  if (length(matches) > 1) stop("more than one file matches ", pattern, " in ", folder)
  if (length(matches) == 0) NA_character_ else matches
}

concat_raw_read_list <- list()
concat_found_amplicon_list <- list()

# Loops over the barcodes and build two tables, one for raw read and one for the amplicons found inside.
for (concat_barcode in concat_barcodes) {
  concat_raw_path <- concat_find_file_f(concat_raw_fastq_dir, sprintf("%s.fastq*", concat_barcode))
  concat_identified_path <- concat_find_file_f(concat_identified_fastq_dir, sprintf("%s_identified.fastq*", concat_barcode))
  if (is.na(concat_raw_path) || is.na(concat_identified_path)) {
    message(concat_barcode, ": file missing, skipped")
    next
  }
  concat_raw_fastq <- concat_read_fastq_f(concat_raw_path)
  concat_raw_read_list[[concat_barcode]] <- tibble(barcode = concat_barcode,
                                                   raw_read_id = sub("^@(\\S+).*", "\\1", concat_raw_fastq$header),
                                                   raw_length = nchar(concat_raw_fastq$sequence),
                                                   read_qs = as.numeric(sub(".*\\bqs:f:([0-9.]+).*", "\\1", concat_raw_fastq$header)))
  concat_identified_fastq <- concat_read_fastq_f(concat_identified_path)
  concat_amplicon_ids <- sub("^@(\\S+).*", "\\1", concat_identified_fastq$header)
  concat_found_amplicon_list[[concat_barcode]] <- tibble(barcode = concat_barcode,
                                                         read_id = concat_amplicon_ids, 
                                                         raw_read_id = sub("_sub\\[.*$", "", concat_amplicon_ids),
                                                         insert_start = as.integer(sub(".*_sub\\[([0-9]+)\\.\\..*", "\\1", concat_amplicon_ids)),
                                                         insert_end = as.integer(sub(".*\\.\\.([0-9]+)\\]$", "\\1", concat_amplicon_ids)))
  cat(sprintf("%s: %s raw reads, %s amplicons\n", concat_barcode, comma(length(concat_raw_fastq$sequence)), comma(length(concat_amplicon_ids))))
}

# Combines the per barcode results, arranges by starting position of amplicons and calculates gaps length from previosu found amplicon
concat_raw_reads <- bind_rows(concat_raw_read_list)
concat_found_amplicons <- bind_rows(concat_found_amplicon_list) %>%
  arrange(barcode, raw_read_id, insert_start) %>%
  group_by(barcode, raw_read_id) %>%
  mutate(found_rank = row_number(), found_size = n(),
         gap_to_previous = insert_start - lag(insert_start)) %>% 
  ungroup()

stopifnot("no barcode had both files" = nrow(concat_raw_reads) > 0,
          "could not read the read quality (qs:f:) from the raw headers" = !anyNA(concat_raw_reads$read_qs),
          "the same amplicon read_id occurs twice in the FASTQ files (a file copied under two barcodes?)" = !anyDuplicated(concat_found_amplicons$read_id))

# one row per raw read with concatemer size and checks how long are the flanking position, for figuring out if its really the right size concatemer or there were just no primers found
concat_raw_read_summary <- concat_raw_reads %>%
  left_join(concat_found_amplicons %>%
              group_by(barcode, raw_read_id) %>%
              summarise(found_size = n(), lead = min(insert_start), last_end = max(insert_end), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("barcode", "raw_read_id")) %>%
  mutate(tail = raw_length - last_end,
         size_group = factor(case_when(is.na(found_size) ~ "none",
                                       found_size >= 10 ~ "10+",
                                       TRUE ~ as.character(found_size)), levels = c("none", 1:9, "10+")))

# Median length of one amplicon
concat_amplicon_unit <- median(concat_found_amplicons$gap_to_previous, na.rm = TRUE) 
# Median length of flank before the first amplicon
concat_typical_lead <- median(concat_raw_read_summary$lead[concat_raw_read_summary$found_size > 1], na.rm = TRUE)
# Median length of flank after the last amplicon
concat_typical_tail <- median(concat_raw_read_summary$tail[concat_raw_read_summary$found_size > 1], na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("typical flanks: %.0f bases before the first amplicon, %.0f after the last; neighbouring amplicons %.0f bases apart\n",
            concat_typical_lead, concat_typical_tail, concat_amplicon_unit))

# Calcualtes cutoffs if median lead is 90 and median length of amplicon 120, cutoff is at 150. if Flanks are lonegr than that there is probably one missed amplicon
concat_lead_cutoff <- concat_typical_lead + concat_amplicon_unit / 2
concat_tail_cutoff <- concat_typical_tail + concat_amplicon_unit / 2

concat_flanks <- concat_raw_read_summary %>%
  filter(!is.na(found_size)) %>%
  mutate(read_type = ifelse(found_size == 1, "Singleton", "In concatemer"),
         missed_amplicon = lead > concat_lead_cutoff | tail > concat_tail_cutoff)
concat_missed_share <- concat_flanks %>%
  group_by(read_type) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), pct_missed = 100 * mean(missed_amplicon), .groups = "drop")
kable(concat_missed_share, digits = 1)

concat_raw_read_summary %>%
  summarise(n = n(), median_length = median(raw_length), median_qs = median(read_qs), .by = size_group) %>%
  arrange(size_group) %>%
  kable(digits = 1)

concat_flanks_long <- concat_flanks %>%
  select(read_type, "Before the first amplicon" = lead, "After the last amplicon" = tail) %>%
  pivot_longer(-read_type, names_to = "flank", values_to = "bases") %>%
  mutate(flank = factor(flank, levels = unique(flank)))

concat_flank_cutoffs <- tibble(flank = unique(concat_flanks_long$flank), cutoff = c(concat_lead_cutoff, concat_tail_cutoff))
concat_flank_axis_end <- quantile(concat_flanks_long$bases, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE)

# Plots using this data
concat_size_group_fill <- c(none = concat_beige, "1" = concat_brown, setNames(rep(concat_sage, 9), c(2:9, "10+")))

p_concat_raw_length <- ggplot(concat_raw_read_summary, aes(x = size_group, y = raw_length, fill = size_group, colour = size_group)) +
  geom_violin(linewidth = 0.4, width = 0.8, scale = "width") + 
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white", linewidth = 0.4) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = concat_size_group_fill, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = concat_darken_f(concat_size_group_fill), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(title = "A  Raw read length by concatemer size",
       subtitle = sprintf("none = no amplicon found; one amplicon adds about %.0f bases", concat_amplicon_unit),
       x = "Concatemer size", y = "Raw read length (bases, log scale)") +
  concat_theme

p_concat_raw_quality <- ggplot(concat_raw_read_summary, aes(x = size_group, y = read_qs, fill = size_group, colour = size_group)) +
  geom_violin(linewidth = 0.4, width = 0.8, scale = "width") + 
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white", linewidth = 0.4) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = concat_size_group_fill, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = concat_darken_f(concat_size_group_fill), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "B  Mean read quality by concatemer size", subtitle = "Mean Phred quality of the whole raw read (QS from the basecaller)",
       x = "Concatemer size", y = "Mean read quality (qs)") +
  concat_theme

p_concat_flanks <- ggplot(concat_flanks_long, aes(x = bases, fill = read_type, colour = read_type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.55, linewidth = 0.4, adjust = 0.6, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_vline(data = concat_flank_cutoffs, aes(xintercept = cutoff), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30") +
  facet_wrap(~ flank, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = concat_group_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = concat_darken_f(concat_group_colours), name = NULL) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, concat_flank_axis_end)) +
  labs(title = "C  Unexplained sequence next to the amplicons",
       subtitle = sprintf("Main normal read end peak (adapter + barcode)\nSmaller peak %.0f bases to the right is one whole amplicon not found,\n%s",
                  concat_amplicon_unit, paste(sprintf("%s %.1f%%", tolower(concat_missed_share$read_type), concat_missed_share$pct_missed), collapse = ", ")),
       x = "Bases", y = "Density") +
  concat_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0), axis.text.y = element_blank())

p_concat_raw_reads <- wrap_plots(wrap_plots(p_concat_raw_length, p_concat_raw_quality, ncol = 1), p_concat_flanks,
                                            ncol = 2, widths = c(1.2, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(title = sprintf("Raw reads and the amplicons found in them (%d barcodes, %s raw reads)",
                                             n_distinct(concat_raw_reads$barcode), comma(nrow(concat_raw_reads))),
                             theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, hjust = 0.5)))
print(p_concat_raw_reads)
ggsave(file.path(concat_out_dir, "raw_reads_length_quality_flanks.png"), p_concat_raw_reads, width = 11.69, height = 8.27, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(concat_out_dir, "raw_reads_length_quality_flanks.pdf"), p_concat_raw_reads, width = 11.69, height = 8.27, device = cairo_pdf)
```

```{r Amplicon_Rank_Adjusted_Heatmaps, eval = params$run_filtration_parameters, fig.width = 8.27, fig.height = 9.5, out.width = "70%"}
# 8. Plot, triangle rank heatmaps for original ranks and adjusted ranks
# computes the corrections for amplicon ranks
concat_fastq_rank_corrections <- concat_found_amplicons %>%
  left_join(select(concat_raw_read_summary, barcode, raw_read_id, lead, tail), by = c("barcode", "raw_read_id")) %>%
  mutate(missed_before = pmax(0, round((lead - concat_typical_lead) / concat_amplicon_unit)),
         missed_gap = pmax(0, round(coalesce(gap_to_previous, concat_amplicon_unit) / concat_amplicon_unit) - 1),
         missed_after = pmax(0, round((tail - concat_typical_tail) / concat_amplicon_unit)),
         adjusted_rank = found_rank + missed_before + cumsum(missed_gap),
         adjusted_size = found_size + missed_before + sum(missed_gap) + missed_after,
         .by = c(barcode, raw_read_id))

# number of missed amplicons added per row
concat_extra <- distinct(concat_fastq_rank_corrections, barcode, raw_read_id, found_size, adjusted_size) %>%
  mutate(extra = adjusted_size - found_size)
cat(sprintf("%s raw reads: adjusted size = found size for %.1f%%, one higher for %.1f%%, two or more higher for %.1f%%\n",
            comma(nrow(concat_extra)), 100 * mean(concat_extra$extra == 0), 100 * mean(concat_extra$extra == 1), 100 * mean(concat_extra$extra >= 2)))

# the reads table rows with their adjusted rank and size from previous concat_fastq_rank_corrections
concat_amplicons_with_adjusted_rank <- concat_amplicons %>%
  inner_join(select(concat_fastq_rank_corrections, read_id, adjusted_rank, adjusted_size), by = "read_id")
cat(sprintf("%s of %s reads table rows matched a FASTQ amplicon (%.1f%%)\n", comma(nrow(concat_amplicons_with_adjusted_rank)),
            comma(nrow(concat_amplicons)), 100 * nrow(concat_amplicons_with_adjusted_rank) / nrow(concat_amplicons)))
stopifnot("almost no reads table row matched the FASTQ files: are they from the same sequencing run?" =
            nrow(concat_amplicons_with_adjusted_rank) >= 0.5 * nrow(concat_amplicons))

# one cell per version, size and rank: the same reads twice, once with the ranks as found and once with the adjusted ranks
concat_rank_cells <- bind_rows(
  "As found by obimultiplex" = select(concat_amplicons_with_adjusted_rank, concatemer_size, concatemer_rank, fate, snp_position_quality),
  "Adjusted for missed amplicons" = select(concat_amplicons_with_adjusted_rank, concatemer_size = adjusted_size, concatemer_rank = adjusted_rank, fate, snp_position_quality), .id = "version") %>%
  filter(concatemer_size <= concat_largest_size_shown) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            pct_used = 100 * mean(fate == "Used for genotyping"),
            pct_below_q = 100 * mean(snp_position_quality < margin_min_snp_quality, na.rm = TRUE),
            .by = c(version, concatemer_size, concatemer_rank)) %>%
  mutate(enough_reads = n >= concat_min_amplicons,
         version = factor(version, levels = unique(version))) 

# Plots
concat_heatmap_theme <- theme_minimal(base_family = plot_font, base_size = 9) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10.5), plot.title.position = "plot",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8.5), axis.text = element_text(size = 6.5),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.title = element_text(size = 8), legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.key.width = unit(3, "mm"))

# Share of amplicons used for genotyping per rank and concatemer size
p_concat_rank_used <- ggplot(concat_rank_cells, aes(x = factor(concatemer_size), y = factor(concatemer_rank))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = ifelse(enough_reads, pct_used, NA)), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(enough_reads, sprintf("%.0f", pct_used), "")), size = 1.9, colour = "grey15") +
  facet_wrap(~ version, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = concat_cream, high = concat_dark_green, na.value = "grey90", name = "%") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "A  Amplicons used for genotyping (%)", x = "Concatemer size", y = "Rank (1 = first amplicon)") +
  concat_heatmap_theme

# # Share of amplicons with SNP base quality below threshold per rank and concatemer size
p_concat_rank_low_quality <- ggplot(concat_rank_cells, aes(x = factor(concatemer_size), y = factor(concatemer_rank))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = ifelse(enough_reads, pct_below_q, NA)), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(enough_reads, sprintf("%.0f", pct_below_q), "")), size = 1.9, colour = "grey15") +
  facet_wrap(~ version, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = concat_cream, high = concat_brown, na.value = "grey90", name = "%") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = sprintf("B  SNP base quality below Q%d (%%)", margin_min_snp_quality), x = "Concatemer size", y = "Rank (1 = first amplicon)") +
  concat_heatmap_theme

p_concat_rank_heatmaps <- wrap_plots(p_concat_rank_used, p_concat_rank_low_quality, ncol = 1) +
  plot_annotation(title = "Every rank inside the concatemer: as found vs adjusted for missed amplicons",
                  subtitle = sprintf("Adjusted = missed amplicons (whole %.0f-base steps of unexplained sequence) counted back in", concat_amplicon_unit),
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
                                plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey30", hjust = 0.5)))
print(p_concat_rank_heatmaps)
ggsave(file.path(concat_out_dir, "quality_by_rank_and_size_adjusted.png"), p_concat_rank_heatmaps, width = 8.27, height = 9.5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
ggsave(file.path(concat_out_dir, "quality_by_rank_and_size_adjusted.pdf"), p_concat_rank_heatmaps, width = 8.27, height = 9.5, device = cairo_pdf)
```
